name: 40033-prefillheavy-qwen3moe30b-1gpu
model: nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4. Public and ungated, ~15 GB on disk: 4-bit NVFP4 weights produced by modelopt, with an fp8 KV cache scheme.
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, no expert parallelism. One in-process engine (guidellm `vllm_python`), no router, no external cache tier.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=16, bounded at 32 requests with a 50% warmup -> 16 warmup and 16 measured, no cooldown. guidellm sizes the warmup as `int(percent * max_requests)`, so 0.5 gives exactly 16: one full wave of the 16 streams is warmup and the next full wave is measured, which keeps the measured window at a constant concurrency of 16 instead of straddling a partial wave. The request COUNT is the one quantity in this card that is not the source's -- it ran 150 measured -- and it is cut for a runner constraint, not a modelling one: this machine kills any run that has not written a report within 900 s, and at this workload's per-request latency 150 requests cannot finish inside that. Everything scored here is a RATE at a fixed concurrency and does not depend on how many requests are issued. `safety_seconds: 420` is a runaway guard sized so the run still writes a report inside the runner's window; it is not a target.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, exactly 2000 prompt tokens and exactly 100 output tokens, min = max on both, greedy at temperature 0.0, seed 40033. Prompts are drawn independently and prefix caching is off, so every request is a real 2000-token prefill; the backend applies the chat template, so the engine's own prompt-token count reads a handful above 2000, and it sets ignore_eos, so every request emits exactly 100 tokens.
purpose: A document-analysis assistant summarizing long reports for 16 concurrent users on a single GPU.
launch:
# The engine's command line. Commit efb4cdf2b8000c850d04706eb6f788903e3ee544; the interpreter and
# the hardware seal are in configs/env.yaml, which is this machine's and is not portable.
# guidellm drives the engine in-process through the `vllm_python` backend, not over HTTP.

model: nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4

# THE MoE HALF OF THE EMULATION PIN, and not what this engine selects here: on an H100 with a
# modelopt NVFP4 checkpoint the native backends come first and `EMULATION` is last in the
# availability list. The dense half is VLLM_NVFP4_GEMM_BACKEND=emulation in configs/tuned.yaml.
# Both halves are required -- setting one leaves the other half of the model on a native kernel,
# silently, with nothing crashing to tell you.
moe-backend: emulation

tensor-parallel-size: 1

# Not the default, and part of the setup: this path is measured in eager mode.
enforce-eager: true

# Do not drop these as "the defaults". They are what `vllm serve` resolves to on a >=70 GiB
# non-A100 device at this commit; the in-process backend does not go through that table and would
# otherwise fall through to 2048 / 128, and 2048 would chunk every 2000-token prompt differently.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024

enable-chunked-prefill: true

# Inert either way (each synthetic prompt is drawn independently, no shared prefix); off
# guarantees all 165 requests are full 2000-token prefills.
enable-prefix-caching: false

# The workload's worst case is 2100 tokens plus the chat template; unset, the engine would take
# the checkpoint's 40960.
max-model-len: 4096

# This engine's own default, written down so a future change of default cannot move the budget.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
